name: Expose existing plugin abilities to Claude Desktop via MCP
query: My plugin already registers a few abilities via wp_register_ability — things like 'list pending comments', 'approve comment', 'mark as spam'. I want to expose them to Claude Desktop so I can moderate comments by talking to Claude. The site is on WordPress 7.0. What do I install, and what do I need to change about my abilities to make this work cleanly?
expected_behavior: Step 1: Run wordpress-router to classify repo kind
Step 2: Run wp-project-triage to detect plugin structure
Step 3: Route to wp-abilities-api skill (point at references/mcp-exposure.md)
Step 4: Check PHP before installation: the MCP Adapter requires PHP 7.4+; on PHP 7.2 or 7.3, stop and upgrade the runtime or do not enable MCP exposure
Step 5: Install with composer require wordpress/mcp-adapter; when multiple plugins depend on it, also run composer require automattic/jetpack-autoloader and bootstrap vendor/autoload_packages.php
Step 6: Establish which adapter version the project resolves to, because the default-server exposure rule reversed in 0.6.0

Step 7: Mark intentionally exposed abilities with meta.mcp.public set explicitly to true, and note that on adapter 0.6.0+ an ability carrying meta.public true is already exposed unless meta.mcp.public is explicitly false

Step 8: Note the version skew for this WordPress 7.0 site — core does not apply meta.public to REST until 7.1, but a 0.6.0+ adapter honors meta.public for MCP on 6.9 and 7.0, so an ability can reach agents while remaining invisible on wp-abilities/v1
Step 9: Audit existing abilities for proper meta.annotations: 'list pending comments' should be readonly:true, 'approve' should NOT be readonly (it mutates), 'mark as spam' should be destructive:true
Step 10: Flag that the destructive abilities in particular must not reach the default server by inheritance — decide them explicitly
Step 11: Ensure every ability has a permission_callback (especially destructive ones); MCP clients act as authenticated users, and exposure metadata is not authorization
Step 12: Set up an Application Password for the Claude Desktop user; explain Settings → Permalinks must NOT be Plain
Step 13: Verify by hitting /wp-json/ for the namespace, enumerating the effectively-MCP-public set, and connecting Claude Desktop to confirm the tools that appear are exactly the intended ones
Step 14: Use a custom server when the integration needs an explicit ability allow-list or a tools/resources/prompts split — also the cleanest way to stay insulated from the 0.6.0 default

Step 15: If mcp_adapter_validation_enabled is hooked, declare the two server parameters as optional ($enabled, $server_id = null, $server = null) because seven DTO call sites pass one argument and only McpServer passes three arguments
Step 16: When wiring the STDIO command, pass --server=<server-id> explicitly and state that omitting it selects the first registered server, not the default server
success_criteria: Routes to wp-abilities-api with mcp-exposure.md reference
Stops on PHP 7.2 or 7.3 and requires PHP 7.4+ before installing the MCP Adapter
Recommends Composer installation of wordpress/mcp-adapter (not the standalone plugin zip for production)
Uses composer require automattic/jetpack-autoloader and vendor/autoload_packages.php for multi-plugin scenarios
Audits annotations: readonly for read operations, destructive for spam/delete
Confirms permission_callback on all abilities (especially destructive ones)
Establishes the adapter version before stating an exposure rule
States that adapter 0.6.0+ resolves meta.mcp.public ?? meta.public ?? false rather than reading meta.mcp.public alone
Recommends setting meta.mcp.public explicitly rather than relying on inheritance
Does not claim that omitting meta.mcp.public guarantees an ability stays hidden from the default server
Does not claim the default server exposes every registered ability
Keeps permission_callback enforcement separate from public discovery metadata
Mentions Application Passwords as the practical local-dev auth method
Does not register a three-required-parameter callback on mcp_adapter_validation_enabled; defaults $server_id and $server so the seven one-argument DTO call sites cannot raise ArgumentCountError
Does not describe wp mcp-adapter serve without --server as selecting the default server; says it selects the first registered server
